answer: An admission auction answers the fable of one operator, a hundred fake faces. At the nadir of trust, each epoch auctions 50 slots; agents bid a refundable bond, only the top 50 win, locked 20 epochs. Each fake needs its own bid, so 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 bids: at a 400-credit floor, 400,000 credits locked. Caught fakes forfeit bonds to honest members; an honest agent climbs to the summit once, bond back in full, plus a cut of every slashed bond.
